subject: Archaeology
title: Cahokia: America's Forgotten City
description: A micro-lesson that makes Cahokia: America's Forgotten City usable.

hook.text: Before Columbus, a city near modern St. Louis had a larger population than London in the year 1100.

buildup.text: Cahokia was home to 20,000 people, with plazas, neighborhoods, and a 100-foot earthen pyramid.

discovery.text: Monks Mound is the largest earthwork in the Americas — bigger at its base than the Great Pyramid of Giza.

twist.text: The city collapsed by 1400. Floods, deforestation, and political unrest likely caused the decline.

climax.text: For centuries, European settlers refused to believe Native Americans built it. They invented lost-race myths.

punchline.text: America's greatest ancient city was ignored because of racism.

quiz.question: What was Monks Mound at Cahokia?
options: A natural hill that the city was built around
The largest earthwork in the Americas, bigger at its base than the Great Pyramid
A burial site containing thousands of artifacts
